clue.text: Annoy by leaving on purpose

parts.note: to be off is to be leaving, as in 'I'm off now'
an end is an aim or purpose, as in 'to that end'

explanation.surface: Someone deliberately walks out in order to irritate another person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'on' are link words joining the definition and the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend someone is to upset or irritate them, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Cheats seen — watch pockets

definitions.meaning: to fob someone off is to trick or cheat them
a fob is a small pocket in a waistcoat or trousers for a pocket watch

explanation.surface: A pickpocket's victims are cheated while somebody watches their pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are dictionary meanings: fob as a verb is to deceive, and as a noun a small watch pocket.

clue.text: Delights in actor's appearances

definitions.meaning: to entrance someone is to delight or enchant them, stress on the second syllable
an actor's ... are the moments they come on stage

explanation.surface: A performer charms the audience every time they step on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between the two definitions; the two senses are pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning enchants, and a noun for the moments a player comes on stage: the same spelling with two pronunciations.

clue.text: Originally, Dickens's Barnaby was a menial

indicators.note: originally points to the very start of the next word, its opening letter

parts.note: Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Charles Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A claim that the hero of a Dickens novel started life as a lowly servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was a' are link words. Barnaby Rudge is Dickens's 1841 novel, so the surname supplies the tail of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A drudge is someone doing hard, dull servile work, the same as a menial used as a noun.

clue.text: Work on icebreaker in a new wet suit

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for work inside the rearranged letters
the breaker part of icebreaker signals that the word ice is broken up and mixed
new tells us the pooled letters are made afresh in a different order

parts.note: OP is the standard abbreviation of opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: An icebreaker ship works on through freezing water while a crew member wears a fresh wetsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'icebreaker' reads as a ship, but it splits: its second half and 'new' are the mixing signals, and 'in' is the container signal. The definition is only 'suit', not 'wet suit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-piece is a suit of matching jacket and trousers or skirt, or a bikini.

clue.text: Members are entitled to sit here

definitions.text: Members are entitled to sit here

parts.words: Members are entitled to sit here
parts.note: reads as a club's rule on who may take a seat, but 'entitled' means holding titles: peers in Parliament's upper chamber

explanation.surface: A notice explaining that members have the right to sit in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entitled' seems to mean having the right, but it means bearing a title, like a lord or baroness, in the upper chamber of the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's upper house of Parliament is made up of members holding peerages, so its members are literally titled.

clue.text: A barrier to progress for some races

definitions.text: A barrier to progress for some races

parts.words: A barrier to progress for some races
parts.note: reads like a remark on prejudice holding back peoples, but means hurdles and hedges set out in a running race of a particular kind

explanation.surface: A grim observation that some ethnic groups face a barrier to advancement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'races' suggests peoples; it means running contests, and an obstacle race is one with things to clamber over.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle is anything that blocks the way, and obstacle races are a named kind of running event.

clue.text: It may make a topping sweet

definitions.text: It may make a topping sweet

parts.words: It may make a topping sweet
parts.note: a sugary coat spread over a cake makes the top sweet; 'topping' also hints at an excellent sweet

explanation.surface: Something that might turn a dessert topping sugary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' can be read as an adjective meaning splendid, but here it is the coat on top of a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar paste spread over a cake is its sweet top layer, the frosting.

clue.text: Prince not getting up for the dance

parts.note: Charles was a long-serving Prince of Wales

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the word not is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A prince stays seated rather than rising to join the dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns NOT into TON, written upward in the grid. 'for the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively 1920s dance named after the city in South Carolina, famous for its swivelling kicks.

clue.text: Busts are being developed beyond comprehension

indicators.note: being developed suggests the letters of busts are being worked up into a new form

explanation.surface: Sculpted busts are under construction and nobody can understand them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being developed' rearranges BUSTS ARE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstruse means obscure and hard to understand, so beyond comprehension is a fair synonym phrase.

clue.text: The continual round of wage increases?

definitions.text: The continual round of wage increases?

parts.words: The continual round of wage increases?
parts.note: describes the economic cycle in which pay rises push up prices, which push up pay again, an ever-winding curve

explanation.surface: A question about the endless cycle of pay rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Economists speak of a wage-price spiral, a curve winding round and round ever higher.

clue.text: Copper isn't very well behaved

definitions.meaning: copper is a lesser metal, not as valuable as the yellow precious metal
the phrase describes a child who has been perfectly good

explanation.surface: A remark that a policeman is not a model of good behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but the first definition is about the metal, worth less than gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a child who behaves perfectly, and literally says something matches the precious metal, which copper does not.

clue.text: Assignment left in a particular spot

indicators.note: in says the letter for left is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a location is a particular place or spot

explanation.surface: A task given to someone is left at a certain place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside A + LOCATION, just after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An allocation is something assigned or allotted, such as a share or task, so it matches assignment.

clue.text: Smart fellow the French take into account

indicators.note: take into tells us the French article goes inside the abbreviation for account

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: French people take a clever man into consideration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart fellow' leans on the phrase smart alec, a know-all; the container signal is 'take into'.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is a know-all, so the name stands for a would-be clever fellow.

clue.text: To act in this way is not in one's own interest

definitions.text: To act in this way is not in one's own interest

parts.words: To act in this way is not in one's own interest
parts.note: describes behaviour that puts others first and ignores personal benefit

explanation.surface: A warning that some behaviour does a person no good.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like advice against foolishness, but it praises acting for others.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with no concern for oneself, putting other people's needs first, is unselfish behaviour.

clue.text: He might take advantage of a damsel in distress

definitions.text: He might take advantage of a damsel in distress

indicators.note: distress suggests the letters of a damsel in are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A warning about a man who would exploit a woman in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distress' rearranges A DAMSEL IN, and the whole clue also describes a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: A womaniser who chases women is exactly the sort who might exploit a damsel in trouble.

clue.text: Switch choices occasionally

definitions.meaning: the two positions a light switch can be in

explanation.surface: Someone changes their mind every now and again.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means intermittently, and literally names the two settings of a switch.

clue.text: Starts career studies

definitions.meaning: to take up a line of work, as in 'enters the law'
examines or investigates, as in looking closely at a matter

explanation.surface: A person begins their working life by taking up studies.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to take up a profession and to look into something in detail.

clue.text: Decline and fall

definitions.meaning: a decrease, as in a decline in prices
to let go and come down, or a descent

explanation.surface: A pairing of near-synonyms, as in the decline and fall of an empire.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a downturn and a fall, a straightforward double synonym.

clue.text: Army leader wearing decoration is quite usual

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer, an army unit's leader
MM is the Military Medal, a British award for bravery
to have something on is to be wearing it

explanation.surface: A commanding officer in his medal is a familiar sight.
explanation.walkthrough: MM, the Military Medal, is a British gallantry award. 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Common means ordinary or frequently met with, so quite usual fits.

clue.text: Unreliable combination of opposites

definitions.meaning: to play the phrase is to behave irresponsibly or inconsistently
fast meaning firmly fixed and loose meaning slack are opposites joined by 'and'

explanation.surface: Something untrustworthy is made by mixing contraries.
explanation.definitionFit: To play the idiom is to be careless and unreliable, and its two adjectives are opposites joined together.

clue.text: A private coach?

parts.note: suggests a hired carriage or bus, but means a teacher giving individual lessons

explanation.surface: A question about a privately hired bus or carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' looks like a vehicle; it is a person who teaches one-to-one.
explanation.definitionFit: A private teacher who coaches a pupil individually, often for exams.

clue.text: In football he must be included in the top eleven players

indicators.note: included in signals that the answer sits inside the words top eleven

explanation.surface: A football star surely deserves a place in the best team of all time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' finds the run in 'toP ELEven'; 'must be' and 'the' and 'players' play no part beyond the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brazilian forward is often named the greatest footballer ever, so he fits a man from football.

clue.text: Way out writer in French restaurant

indicators.note: out places the writer on the outside of the abbreviation for way

parts.note: Biro is a British brand name for a ballpoint pen, used for any such pen
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A far-out author dines in a Parisian eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way out' looks like an exit or 'far out', but 'out' puts BIRO outside ST. A Biro is the everyday British word for a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant of the kind associated with France.

clue.text: Recall soldiers and arm

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
an arm is a limb, also called a member

explanation.surface: An order to call back troops and weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common crossword abbreviation for soldiers. 'arm' suggests a weapon, but it is a limb. 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To remember is to call something back to mind, the same as recall.

clue.text: Strange surgery involving female implants

indicators.note: involving says the anagram wraps round the letter for female
surgery suggests the letters of strange are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd operation fits a woman with implants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' looks like the anagram signal, but it is the fodder; 'surgery' rearranges STRANGE, and 'involving' puts F inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To engraft is to graft or implant tissue, so engrafts is a synonym of implants as a verb.

clue.text: Grandma gets setback in French town

parts.note: nan is an informal British word for grandmother

indicators.note: back tells us the letters of set are read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly woman suffers a reverse while visiting France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' looks like one word meaning a reverse; split it, so its second half is the turnaround signal. 'gets' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a large city in western France on the Loire.
